name: Nayapul
description: Trek starting point by the Modi Khola river

name: Tikhedhunga
description: Small village with basic teahouses. The trail involves a steep climb up stone steps through rhododendron forests.

name: Ulleri
description: Known for the iconic stone staircase (3380 steps). Great spot for a rest break before continuing to Ghorepani.

name: Ghorepani
description: Popular stop with panoramic mountain views. Base for the early morning Poon Hill hike. Numerous teahouses and lodges available.

name: Poon Hill Viewpoint
description: Sunrise viewpoint at 3,210m offering 360-degree views of Annapurna, Dhaulagiri, Manaslu, and Machhapuchhre ranges.

name: Tadapani
description: A scenic ridge-top village with excellent mountain views. Trail passes through dense rhododendron and oak forests.

name: Chhomrong
description: A beautiful Gurung village with stone-paved streets and stunning views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli. Last major settlement before entering the sanctuary.

name: Sinuwa
description: Small settlement perched on a ridge. Trail descends to the Chhomrong Khola before climbing steeply through bamboo forests.

name: Bamboo
description: A cluster of teahouses surrounded by dense bamboo forests. A peaceful stop with the sound of the nearby river.

name: Dovan
description: A small clearing with teahouses where the valley narrows. The trail continues alongside the river through dense forest.

name: Himalaya Hotel
description: A popular teahouse stop despite its grand name. Trail continues through increasingly alpine terrain with fewer trees.

name: Deurali
description: The last stop before the base camp. The landscape becomes stark and alpine with moraines and snow-capped peaks all around.

name: Machhapuchhre Base Camp
description: Base camp for the sacred Mt. Machhapuchhre. The trail traverses a landslide area with spectacular views of the surrounding peaks.

name: Annapurna Base Camp
description: The ultimate destination at 4,130m. Surrounded by a natural amphitheater of peaks including Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Gangapurna, and Machhapuchhre.

name: Chhomrong (return)
description: Return route descending back through Bamboo, Sinuwa to Chhomrong.

name: Jhinu Danda
description: Famous for natural hot springs (tatopani) by the river. A perfect way to relax after the trek. Trail descends steeply from Chhomrong.

name: Nayapul (return)
description: Final leg back to Nayapul passing through Landruk and along the Modi Khola river.

name: Lukla
description: Gateway to the Everest region. A thrilling flight from Kathmandu lands at one of the world's most dramatic airports.

name: Phakding
description: First day's walk takes you through pine forests and across suspension bridges along the Dudh Koshi River.

name: Namche Bazaar
description: The bustling Sherpa capital of the Khumbu region. A steep climb leads to this horseshoe-shaped town with shops, bakeries, and amazing mountain views.

name: Tyangboche
description: Home to the famous Tengboche Monastery, the largest in the Khumbu region. Offers stunning views of Everest, Ama Dablam, and Lhotse.

name: Dingboche
description: A beautiful settlement in a valley surrounded by towering peaks. Used as an acclimatization stop with a hike to Nagarjun Hill.

name: Lobuche
description: The last permanent settlement before Everest Base Camp. Located in a stark, alpine landscape surrounded by glaciers and moraines.

name: Gorakshep
description: The final stop before Everest Base Camp. From here, trekkers make the journey to base camp and the early morning hike to Kala Patthar.

name: Everest Base Camp
description: The ultimate destination at 5,364m. Stand at the foot of the world's tallest mountain. Best visited in the afternoon after arriving from Gorakshep.

name: Kala Patthar
description: A 5,555m viewpoint offering the best panoramic views of Mount Everest, Nuptse, and the surrounding Himalayan giants.

name: Pheriche
description: Return route descending through Lobuche to Pheriche, a village known for its medical research station and stunning valley setting.

name: Syabrubesi
description: Starting point of the Langtang Valley trek. A small town on the Trisuli River with basic amenities and stunning surrounding hills.

name: Lama Hotel
description: A small settlement deep in the forest. The trail follows the Langtang River through bamboo and rhododendron forests with occasional glimpses of langur monkeys.

name: Langtang Village
description: The main village in the Langtang Valley, rebuilt after the 2015 earthquake. Offers stunning views of Langtang Lirung and an opportunity to experience Tamang culture.

name: Kyanjin Gompa
description: The end of the trekking route at 3,870m. Features a famous monastery, cheese factory, and stunning views of Langtang Lirung, Genjumpa, and Tserko Ri.

name: Kyanjin Ri
description: A challenging but rewarding hike to 4,773m offering panoramic views of the Langtang range and into Tibet.

name: Nayapul
description: Starting point for the Ghorepani Poon Hill trek.

name: Tikhedhunga
description: First overnight stop. Steep climb through terraced fields and small settlements with mountain views.

name: Ulleri
description: Famous for its massive stone staircase. A challenging but rewarding ascent through rhododendron forests.

name: Ghorepani
description: Main overnight stop and base for the Poon Hill sunrise hike. Offers excellent views of the Dhaulagiri and Annapurna ranges.

name: Poon Hill Viewpoint
description: The highlight of the trek. A pre-dawn hike to 3,210m rewards you with one of the best Himalayan sunrise views in Nepal.

name: Tadapani
description: Descend through rhododendron forests to this ridge-top village with spectacular mountain views.

name: Landruk
description: Traditional Gurung village with charming stone houses and terraced fields. Offers a glimpse into rural Nepali life.

name: Nayapul (return)
description: Final leg back to Nayapul along the Modi Khola riverbank.
